newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Capricornia says nickel strike may extend.
newsitem.headline: Capricornia says nickel strike may extend.

text.p: Drilling at the Emily Ann nickel discovery in Western Australia has confirmed mineralisation over a strike length of 600 metres, Capricorn Resources Australia Ltd said on Thursday.
And it was likely the strike could be extended by another 200 metres, the company said in its quarterly report to June 30.
The latest results followed an accelerated exploration programme during the June quarter at Emily Ann, within the Roundtop joint venture, it said.
Capricorn holds a 25 percent stake in the Roundtop joint venture, a grouping of four prospects some 450 km southeast of Perth.
South Africa's Gencor Ltd holds 37.5 percent of the venture. as does the Forrestania Gold division of Canada's Lionore Mining International Ltd.
Capricorn also said exploration pointed to two new gold discoveries, one in South Australia's Gawler Craton and the other near Coolgardie in Western Australia.

Intersections including 13 metres at 7.4 grams per tonne of gold from 171 metres had been found below the 100-year-old Bird-in-Hand mine at the Woodside goldfield on the eastern margin of the Gawler Craton, it said.
Further exploration would be carried out in the current quarter.
